name: Animal trypanosomiasis (nagana), carried by tsetse flies
_doc: challenge (0 to 1) is how strongly the vector pressures a tile: the product of the range conditions and the climate and vegetation envelope (sim/geography/content_rules.py). A host's loss in a year is annual_loss_at_full_challenge times the challenge. Hosts are herd animal ids (data/world/geography/resources/animals.json); an animal not listed is not a host.
range_note: The range box is the sub-Saharan distribution of Glossina; it also covers Madagascar and the Arabian south-west, which carry no tsetse, so those tiles are over-counted where wet enough. A species distribution is a biogeographic fact (dispersal), not a climate response, so it is data rather than derived.

range.source: Ford and Katondo 1977 Maps of tsetse fly (Glossina) distribution in Africa; Rogers and Robinson 2004 Tsetse distribution, in The Trypanosomiases

challenge_envelope.source: Rogers 1979 and Rogers and Randolph 1986 on tsetse mortality and temperature (survival falls steeply outside about 16-34 C, best near 20-30 C); belt edge near the 500-600 mm isohyet and the need for woodland or thicket cover (Ford 1971 The Role of the Trypanosomiases in African Ecology); kept as a flat optimum above a small cover share

hosts.cattle.source: Losses of trypanosusceptible cattle in high-challenge areas without drugs run from a fifth to well over a third of the herd a year plus lost calves (Swallow 2000 Impacts of Trypanosomiasis on African Agriculture, PAAT Technical and Scientific Series 2; Murray et al. 1982 on N'Dama trypanotolerance). Half a herd a year at full challenge is a mid-high reading. Trypanotolerant breeds exist and are not modelled.

hosts.horse.source: Horses and donkeys are far more susceptible than cattle; infection is near-uniformly fatal untreated (Connor and Van den Bossche 2004 African animal trypanosomiasis, in Infectious Diseases of Livestock)
